verdict.line: You lose if you stand and auto-trade through a full Grit bar and a charged Haymaker heal; you win if you E-pull into an edge-of-Decimate Q, strip his sustain with W, and close with a 5-stack Guillotine before he resets.

brief.thesis: Darius and Sett are both attrition duelists who win the lane through resource management, not burst: Darius refreshes Hemorrhage stacks toward a true-damage execute, Sett fills his Grit bar toward an empowered auto and heals off (W) Haymaker. Whoever denies the other's resource first wins the extended trade, which is why the head-to-head sits razor-close at 49.4% over 1,086 games with EVEN lane and solo-kill grades. Your one lever the data hands you is that Darius (W) directly cuts the healing Sett's whole trade pattern depends on.

theirWindow.when: grit bar full or W charging
theirWindow.what: His next auto is empowered for bonus max-HP damage, and a released Haymaker heals him hard — back off or bait it onto a minion instead of trading into it.

yourWindow.what: All-in immediately: E (Apprehend) to lock him, edge-of-blade Q for the doubled heal, W to cut his sustain, then R once stacks are maxed for the true-damage execute.

start.why: 77.2% pick and the higher-sample line (1,045 games at 50% WR) — front-loads AD so your early autos and Hemorrhage ticks keep pace with Sett's auto-heavy kit rather than trying to out-poke him.

boots.why: 86.7% pick at 50.5% WR — Sett's damage is almost entirely delivered through basic attacks (Q-empowered autos, the Grit-empowered auto, raw AA), so flat AA reduction outvalues Mercury's Treads unless you're facing hard CC stacking elsewhere.

core.why: Highest-winrate path listed (62.1% over 95 games) — the active's AD and haste burst is what wins the all-in window (E-pull into edge-Q into W) before Sett's Grit bar refills.
Adds HP to keep pace with Sett's max-health-scaling Pit Grit passive, while the charge-up slow lets you stick through his E stun setup or catch him mid-Haymaker charge.
Converts his empowered-auto and Haymaker burst into a damage-over-time you can outlast, then the omnivamp lets you win the follow-up fight after his sustain window closes.

situational.when: the enemy team stacks magic damage on top of Sett and steelcaps alone isn't enough
you want the built-in slow and waveclear over Ghostblade's burst (the alternate 60% WR path)
you're dying to his burst before your own combo lands and need the shield to survive to R range

runes.keystoneWhy: Both champions want extended, attrition-style fights rather than single burst windows — Conqueror's stacking heal keeps you even with Sett's W lifesteal-like sustain during the trade instead of losing the war of attrition.

summoners.why: The dominant pick at 72.5% (49.7% WR) — Ghost lets you close the gap on a kiting Sett or run down a Haymaker-charged disengage that Apprehend alone can't reach. Flash+Ignite (49.4%, 20.3% pick) is the better call specifically when you want to punish his W's self-heal directly with the healing-reduction from Ignite in a level 2-3 all-in.

playing.title: Start W, not Q
playing.detail: The 50.9%-WR order takes (W) first, applying the healing-reduction debuff on your first trade — it directly cuts the sustain Sett's whole W-Haymaker pattern depends on, before you even have Apprehend online.

playing.title: Hit the edge of Decimate
playing.detail: Landing (Q) at max range on Sett doubles the heal-back you get compared to hitting him at the center — this is the single highest-value habit in the matchup per OP.GG's own tip.

playing.title: Track the Grit bar, not just HP
playing.detail: Sett's white passive bar fills from champion damage taken; once it's full his next auto is empowered against your max HP. Bait it onto a minion or disengage rather than eating it during a trade.

playing.title: Punish the Haymaker charge
playing.detail: While he holds (W) to charge Haymaker he's committed and slowed relative to a normal trade — an immediate E (Apprehend) pull or all-in denies the extra range and heal he gets from releasing it fully charged.

playing.title: Bank stacks before you R
playing.detail: Hold Hemorrhage at 4-5 stacks before using (R) — Noxian Guillotine's true damage scales directly with stack count and can close out the fight before his W heal has time to matter.

playing.title: Respect the level 6+ grab
playing.detail: Sett's (R) deals more damage the further he carries you — fight in open lane rather than near brush or walls that extend the throw distance once he hits 6.

playing.title: Front-load Youmuu's for the all-in
playing.detail: Rush Ghostblade before Dead Man's Plate — its active is what wins your all-in window in the 9-13 range before his HP-scaling Pit Grit passive starts out-tanking your damage late.

brief.patchCaveat: The build order, rune pages, boots, and summoner picks above are pulled directly from measured Darius vs Sett games on the current patch (1,086-game sample, 49.4% WR, EVEN lane grade); the mechanical reasoning, timings, and trade-pattern analysis are my own read of both kits, not sourced from OP.GG.

stats.opponentTip: Avoid being hit at the center of Sett’s (W) when fighting him. Maintain your passive stacks while hitting him at the edge of [Q] to deal damage.
